item.title: A 0.8B Model, 4GB VRAM, Turned Into a Decision Engine: I Reconciled the Two Number Sets in Unsloth's New Feature
item.description: Unsloth added a 'Decision model' capability to its fine-tuning stack: turn a small LLM like Qwen3.5 0.8B into an engine that emits option probabilities only, trainable in 4GB VRAM. Their own X post carries two sets of numbers (20.7%->74.3% and 30-37%->78%); I reconciled both against the official docs line by line. They are two different baselines that align once you split them. Includes a full-model VRAM/time table and a reproduction trap (start r=16, reproduce with r=64).

item.title: 2.78 Trillion Parameters, 29GB RAM, Half a Token Per Second: Kimi K3 Actually Runs on a Laptop
item.description: WASTE, a pure-C inference engine, squeezes the 2.78-trillion-parameter Kimi K3 into a 64GB laptop: a 982GB container streams expert weights from disk on demand, measured at 0.5 tok/s. Half a token per second is absurdly slow — but it proves running trillion-scale models locally is an engineering problem, not a money problem.
